content.title: About
content.content: Bread, cornmeal and molasses, toasted is a classic American hot cereal often marketed under names like "Malt-O-Meal". The dry flakes are made from whole wheat, cornmeal and molasses, then lightly toasted to give a nutty aroma and a crisp texture. They are typically reconstituted with hot milk or water and served with fruit, nuts or honey.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The first commercial version appeared in the United States in the early 1920s.
The combination of cornmeal and molasses provides natural sweetness without added sugar.
Toasting the flakes enhances flavor and extends shelf life.
It is a popular choice for children's breakfasts because of its soft texture after preparation.
In some regions it is called "milk cereal" due to the traditional way of serving it with milk.

items.title: Source of complex carbohydrates
items.content: Whole wheat and cornmeal deliver slow‑releasing energy, helping to maintain satiety.

items.title: Contains iron
items.content: Molasses contributes a modest amount of iron, supporting blood formation.

items.title: Provides B‑vitamins
items.content: The cereal supplies B1, B3 and folate, which are important for metabolism.

items.title: Provides dietary fiber
items.content: Cornmeal adds fiber that promotes healthy digestion.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: Unlike many ready‑to‑eat cereals, this product is low in fat when prepared with water or low‑fat milk.

items.title: Gluten allergy
items.content: Contains wheat, so it is unsuitable for people with celiac disease or gluten sensitivity.

items.title: Sugar content
items.content: Molasses gives natural sweetness, but those monitoring blood sugar should watch portion size.

items.title: Caloric increase with add‑ins
items.content: Adding milk, cream, or extra sweeteners raises the calorie count significantly.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Pour 240 ml of hot milk or water over the flakes, let stand 2–3 minutes, then top with fruit, berries, nuts or honey to taste. It can also be prepared in the microwave: 1 minute on high, then stir.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep in a sealed container in a cool, dry place. Once opened, use within 4–6 weeks. Discard if any off‑odor, mold, or discoloration appears.

content.title: About
content.content: French and Vienna breads are traditional white loaves made from wheat flour, water, yeast, and salt. They are known for their crisp crust, soft airy crumb, and a distinctive aroma that develops during a long steam‑baked bake.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The classic French baguette is typically 65–70 cm long and weighs about 250 g.
Vienna bread is often called a “pretzel loaf” because of its characteristic twisted shape.
Both breads traditionally undergo a slow fermentation of up to 24 hours, which enhances flavor and crumb structure.
Paris enforces the “Décret Pain” law that defines the composition of traditional French bread: at least 80 % wheat flour, water, yeast and salt, with no additives.
In Austria, Vienna bread is commonly served with butter and jam for breakfast.

items.title: Source of carbohydrates
items.content: Bread provides a quick source of energy through complex carbohydrates that are released gradually into the bloodstream.

items.title: Contains B‑vitamins
items.content: Wheat flour is rich in thiamine (B1), niacin (B3) and folate, which support metabolism and nervous system function.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: Bread supplies iron, magnesium and selenium, important for blood formation and antioxidant protection.

items.title: Dietary fiber (in whole‑grain versions)
items.content: Choosing whole‑grain French or Vienna bread adds dietary fiber that promotes healthy digestion.

items.title: Satiety support
items.content: The combination of carbs and a modest amount of protein helps keep you feeling full longer.

items.title: Gluten
items.content: Wheat bread contains gluten, which can trigger reactions in people with celiac disease or gluten sensitivity.

items.title: High glycemic index
items.content: White French and Vienna breads can raise blood sugar quickly, which may be undesirable for diabetics.

items.title: Salt content
items.content: Traditional recipes often contain a fair amount of salt; those monitoring sodium should limit portions.

items.title: Preservatives in industrial bread
items.content: Some mass‑produced loaves may include additives and preservatives that are not always desirable.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Bread can be enjoyed fresh, toasted, with butter, cheese, cold cuts, or as the base for sandwiches and bruschetta. It pairs well with soups, salads and pâtés. For a healthier option, choose whole‑grain or rye varieties.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store bread in a paper bag or bread box at room temperature for up to 3 days. For longer storage, freeze it in an airtight bag – it will keep flavor and texture for up to 2 months. Thaw at room temperature or briefly warm in the oven before serving.

infant-formula-similac-isomil-soy-ready-.title: Infant formula, Similac Isomil Soy, ready-to-feed

content.title: About
content.content: Similac Isomil Soy is a ready-to-feed soy-based infant formula designed for newborns and infants who are intolerant to lactose or cow's milk protein. It provides a carefully balanced blend of nutrients—including protein, fat, carbohydrates, vitamins, and minerals—essential for a child's growth and development.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The formula is completely ready to use – no water mixing required.
Soy-based protein offers an alternative for babies with cow's milk allergy.
Each container holds 368 ml of product, making it convenient for travel.
Enriched with DHA and ARA, fatty acids important for brain and eye development.
Clinically tested to confirm safety and efficacy.

items.title: Supports growth
items.content: A balanced mix of macro‑ and micronutrients promotes normal growth and development.

items.title: Rich source of protein
items.content: Soy protein is easily digestible and provides essential amino acids.

items.title: Contains DHA and ARA
items.content: These omega‑fatty acids are crucial for brain and visual system development.

items.title: Lactose‑free
items.content: Suitable for infants with lactose intolerance.

items.title: Vitamins and minerals
items.content: Includes iron, calcium, vitamin D, and other nutrients important for bone health and immunity.

items.title: Soy allergy
items.content: Some infants may develop an allergic reaction to soy proteins.

items.title: Not a complete breast milk substitute
items.content: Should be used as an alternative only under pediatric guidance.

items.title: Sugar content
items.content: Contains added carbohydrates like most infant formulas; monitor intake for children prone to cavities.

items.title: Post‑opening storage
items.content: After opening, keep the container refrigerated and use within 48 hours.

content.title: How to Use
content.content: Serve the ready-to-feed formula at room temperature. If desired, chill in the refrigerator. Do not heat in a microwave to avoid hot spots. Offer small amounts and observe the infant’s response.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store unopened containers in a cool, dry place away from direct sunlight. After opening, refrigerate and use within 48 hours. Discard if the product develops an off‑smell, color, or taste.

content.title: About
content.content: Oat bran is the outer layer of the oat grain, rich in fiber and nutrients. When cooked it forms a thick, slightly creamy porridge often enjoyed as a breakfast or added to dishes.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Oat bran contains more dietary fiber than whole oat flakes.
Bran is a by‑product of processing oats for whole grain cereals and flour.
In many traditional cuisines bran is used to make thick soups and porridges.
Oat bran can help lower cholesterol thanks to its beta‑glucan content.
Cooking expands the volume of bran, helping to keep you feeling full longer.

items.title: High in fiber
items.content: Fiber supports digestion, promotes regular bowel movements, and nourishes gut microbiota.

items.title: Contains beta‑glucan
items.content: Beta‑glucan helps reduce LDL‑cholesterol levels in the blood.

items.title: Source of B‑vitamins
items.content: Bran provides thiamine, niacin, and folate, which are essential for energy metabolism.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: It supplies iron, magnesium, zinc, and phosphorus, important for bones and metabolism.

items.title: Low glycemic index
items.content: Cooked bran raises blood sugar slowly, making it suitable for glucose control.

items.title: Gluten sensitivity
items.content: Oats are often processed on equipment that also handles wheat, so people with celiac disease should choose certified gluten‑free bran.

items.title: Digestive discomfort
items.content: Large servings may cause bloating and gas due to the high fiber content.

items.title: Phytic acid
items.content: Bran contains phytic acid, which can reduce mineral absorption if consumed in excess.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Cook bran in water or milk for 5–10 minutes until tender; add fruit, nuts, honey, or spices. It can also be used as a thickener in soups, sauces, and baked goods.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store bran in an airtight container in a cool, dry place. For longer shelf life keep it in the refrigerator or freezer to prevent fat oxidation.

peanut-butter-and-jelly-sandwich-frozen-.title: Peanut Butter and Jelly Sandwich (Frozen, No Crusts)

content.title: About
content.content: A frozen commercial peanut butter and jelly sandwich without crusts is designed for quick preparation. The sandwich is assembled from soft white bread spread evenly with peanut butter and sweet fruit jelly, then frozen to preserve flavor and texture until heating.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Frozen crust‑less sandwiches are popular in school cafeterias and fast‑service eateries.
Peanut butter provides a good source of plant protein and heart‑healthy monounsaturated fats.
Jelly is typically made from berry or fruit purées, often with a modest amount of added sugar.
Freezing helps maintain microbiological safety without the need for preservatives.
The sandwich is usually served after a short microwave heating, making the bread soft and the filling warm.

items.title: Rich in plant protein
items.content: Peanut butter contains about 25 % protein, supporting muscle maintenance.

items.title: Source of healthy fats
items.content: Monounsaturated and polyunsaturated fats in peanut butter promote cardiovascular health.

items.title: Contains B‑vitamins
items.content: Fruit jelly provides vitamin B6 and niacin, important for metabolism.

items.title: Moderate sugar content
items.content: When formulated properly, the jelly supplies energy without causing a sharp glucose spike.

items.title: Convenient and fast
items.content: The frozen product is ready to eat in 1–2 minutes in a microwave, saving preparation time.

items.title: Peanut allergy
items.content: Peanut butter can trigger severe allergic reactions in susceptible individuals.

items.title: Sugar content
items.content: Jelly may contain added sugar; people with diabetes should monitor portion size.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: The sandwich is energy‑dense, so moderate consumption is advised.

items.title: Texture after heating
items.content: Improper heating can make the bread overly soggy or dry.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Heat the frozen sandwich in a microwave for 30–45 seconds on high power or in an oven at 180 °C for 5–7 minutes until the bread is soft and the filling is warm. Serve immediately; optional sides include fresh fruit or vegetables.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the frozen sandwich at –18 °C or lower. After thawing, consume within 2 hours and do not leave at room temperature for more than 1 hour.

rice-brown-with-carrots-dark-green-veget.title: Rice with carrots, dark green vegetables, and tomato sauce

content.title: About
content.content: This dish consists of whole‑grain brown rice cooked with carrots, dark green vegetables (such as broccoli or spinach) and a tomato‑based sauce. The combination provides a balanced mix of complex carbohydrates, fiber, vitamins, and minerals.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Brown rice retains the bran and germ, making it more nutritious than white rice.
Carrots are rich in beta‑carotene, which the body converts to vitamin A.
Dark green vegetables contain chlorophyll and high amounts of vitamin K.
Tomato sauce made from ripe tomatoes is a good source of lycopene, a powerful antioxidant.
The dish can be easily adapted for vegetarian or vegan diets.

items.title: Supports digestion
items.content: Fiber from whole rice and vegetables promotes regular bowel movements and helps prevent constipation.

items.title: Rich source of vitamins
items.content: Beta‑carotene from carrots, vitamin K from greens, and vitamin C from tomatoes support immunity and skin health.

items.title: May reduce cardiovascular risk
items.content: Complex carbs and plant antioxidants help regulate cholesterol levels and blood pressure.

items.title: Eye health
items.content: Beta‑carotene and lycopene contribute to protecting the eyes from age‑related changes.

items.title: Sustained energy
items.content: Slow‑release glucose from brown rice provides lasting satiety and stable energy levels.

items.title: Rice allergy
items.content: A small number of people may be allergic to rice, experiencing skin rashes or digestive symptoms.

items.title: Oxalate content
items.content: Dark green vegetables like spinach contain oxalates, which can contribute to kidney stone formation in susceptible individuals.

items.title: Sodium in sauce
items.content: Tomato sauce often contains added salt; those monitoring sodium intake should choose a low‑salt version.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the dish hot as a main course or as a side to meat, fish, or tofu. Fresh herbs (parsley, basil) can be added for aroma. For extra crunch, sprinkle with pumpkin seeds or toasted nuts.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the prepared dish in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3‑4 days. When frozen, it can be stored for up to 2 months after cooling and placing in a freezer‑safe bag.
